title: Local fights help cancel $260 billion in U.S. data center projects
source_used: Heatmap News (original report of 6 Oct 2026; read in full). The Quartz page of 16 Oct 2026 was blocked (403) and not read.
key_facts: At least $260 billion of data-centre investment was cancelled this year after sustained local opposition, according to Heatmap Pro data (Heatmap News).
About $130 billion, half of the total, was cancelled in the three months ending 30 Sep 2026; third-quarter cancellations exceeded all data-centre projects cancelled last year.
Roughly $1 trillion of data-centre investment faces sustained or meaningful local opposition; about half of projects meeting backlash this year were ultimately cancelled.
Heatmap says the figures have not been published before, are larger than other estimates and are likely an undercount, because only about 60 percent of projects disclose their investment size.
Most cancelled projects failed to get a local permit or faced hostile local-government action; hundreds of US counties and towns now have a ban or moratorium on data-centre construction.

Mitch Jones, policy director at Food and Water Watch, an environmental group that opposes AI data centres, welcomed the figure; a spokesperson for the industry group Data Center Coalition did not respond before press time.
Our 7 Oct 2026 edition carried this Heatmap report (item 38, score 8); Quartz repeated the $260 billion figure on 16 Oct 2026.
quote_evidence: At least $260 billion of data center investments were canceled this year after sustained local opposition, according to new Heatmap Pro data.
About $130 billion in data center investment — or about half of the total — was canceled in the three months ending on September 30.
Roughly $1 trillion in data center investment now faces some kind of sustained or meaningful local opposition, according to Heatmap Pro data.
why_it_matters_hint: Local opposition is now stopping real money: a quarter of a trillion dollars of projects, by one outlet's own count.
event_date: Heatmap report 6 Oct 2026 (our 7 Oct 2026 edition); Quartz repeat 16 Oct 2026
notes: Older news repeated: the figure is Heatmap's own survey, first reported on 6 Oct 2026 and run in our 7 Oct 2026 edition at score 8. The Quartz article (16 Oct 2026) was blocked, so any new detail in it is unknown; its headline carries the same $260 billion. Credit goes to Heatmap News as the first reporter.
